Snake lattice · from flat to dome or saddle

Change the joint angles span by span and the flat lattice becomes a dome or a saddle

Two ways to choose the change. Two levels: one value for the inner spans and the opposite for the outer ones, up to ±30%. Optimized: a value per span, fitted to a target surface. The last switch shows the same case with the crossing springs as they were before the fix, when the model was not four-fold symmetric.

What to notice

    Every step as a table
    Lengths are in lattice units (span chord 1, wave amplitude 0.25). A curvature change of c multiplies the rest curvature at each of a span's seven joints by 1 + c: a negative change flattens the S-wave and the span extends, a positive one curls it and the span contracts. Inner spans are those with both end crossings off the boundary. Height is the highest crossing minus the lowest, measured from the best-fit plane. Curvatures come from a quadratic fit to the crossings. Every run starts from the exact flat lattice. The model has no contact.
